text:
alex: Quick callout — I sketched a proposal for per-org rate limits that allows a small burst window decoupled from sustained RPM/TPM. Putting it here for feedback.

maria: +1 please paste the sketch. Curious how this interacts with concurrency caps and dedicated customers.

alex: Paste: 
```
policy {
  sustained_tpm: 12000   # tokens per minute baseline
  burst_tpm: 36000       # allowed for short bursts (3x)
  burst_window_seconds: 30
  concurrency_limit: 200  # per-org concurrent generation streams
  cooldown_seconds: 60    # after burst window, roll back to sustained
}
```

jin: Quick thoughts: - Burst window lets bursty product traffic (e.g., studio exports) avoid 429s. - Need to ensure billing meters tokens during burst vs sustained correctly.

samir: Concern: third-party clients may spin up many connections to circumvent concurrency caps. We should rate-limit per-key + enforce connection count per API key.

alex: Agreed. Proposal includes two enforcement axes: per-org token rate (TPM) and per-key concurrency. For orgs with multiple keys, tokens aggregated at org level, concurrency enforced per key.

maria: How do we handle Dedicated or Private customers who expect higher guarantees? We probably need policy flags that mark "reserved" capacity and disable burst enforcement.

alex: Yes — policy has a mode: STANDARD | RESERVED. RESERVED bypasses burst throttling, but still applies soft concurrency caps for fairness.

jin: Telemetry: we should emit events `rate_limited`, `burst_start`, `burst_end`, `concurrency_blocked` with fields: org_id, key_id, reason, allowed_tokens, used_tokens. Those will feed console dashboard and alerting.

samir: Agreed on telemetry. Also add `policy_version` so we can hot-swap rules and trace regressions.

alex: Rollout plan idea: 1) Simulate policy in dry-run for 2 weeks (log-only) 2) Canary apply to 5% of orgs (low-usage) 3) Expand to 25% with auto-rollback on >1% error delta 4) Global switch by product signoff.

maria: For UI/console: show current effective limits (sustained, burst, concurrency) + recent burst usage histogram + top offending keys. Also auto-suggest optimizing actions (bundle keys, increase plan).

jin: Edge cases: - orgs with many subteams sharing a single key: aggregator will show noisy spikes. We should recommend key per service in docs. - replayed requests: need idempotency token checks at gateway to avoid double-counting tokens during retries.

samir: How do we compute tokens for streaming responses? If a stream is open and sending tokens, do we count tokens as they are generated? If so, concurrency may be high while token accounting stays low initially.

alex: Count tokens as emitted. Concurrency counts active streams. That means a long-lived stream (low throughput) still occupies concurrency slot; tradeoff intentional to prevent resource exhaustion. We can add a long_streams quota type later.

maria: Billing nuance: when burst is used, bill at normal per-token rate but include a "burst surcharge" metric for internal cost analysis. Customers won't see surcharge unless we change pricing. We need to communicate in docs.

jin: Implementation detail: Gateway should check org token bucket (sustained refill rate = sustained_tpm/60 per second; burst bucket size = burst_tpm * burst_window_seconds/60). Also enforce concurrency via atomic counter in redis with short TTL per connection.

samir: Redis atomic counters sound fine but watch out for thundering herd on large orgs. Consider sharded counters per connection range. Also set backpressure on gateway proxies instead of outright 429s for some low-priority routes.

alex: Backpressure mechanism: return 202 Accepted + `x-backpressure-retry-after` header for non-interactive routes, immediate 429 for interactive/chat endpoints with low latency budgets.

maria: UX: console should have simulation toggle so customers can preview how new limits would affect traffic. Useful for sales/SEs during migrations.

jin: Migration strategy: for existing global quotas, we map org -> sustained_tpm proportional to historical 95th percentile consumption + buffer. Notify customers 2 weeks before enforcement. Provide a self-serve increase flow via console and support override for enterprise deals.

samir: Test plan: unit tests for token math, integration test with gateway + redis on failover, chaos test with synthetic clients. Also run a load test that mimics 1% of all-prod traffic to validate burst behavior.

alex: One more: abuse detection. If `burst_start` events show repeated cycles >N/day, flag org and require rate plan review. Could auto-disable burst after threshold.

maria: LGTM. Can someone open a brief RFC with the config schema, telemetry fields, and rollout checklist? Jin, you owning telemetry? Samir, infra implications? Alex to write initial RFC.

jin: I'll take telemetry. Expect event schema in the RFC.

samir: I'll scope infra changes (redis sharding + backpressure headers).

alex: I'll draft RFC today and link it here. Thanks folks.
